builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning
summary: Replaces full Chronos-2 inference (and its amortized pretraining carbon cost) with a structurally pruned TSFM using a gradient-free criterion to drop one encoder block, versus supervised standalone models that need periodic retraining. Costs a 7.9% parameter reduction (6-9% FLOPs, CO2, and latency savings) with no retraining overhead, and requires choosing between TSFM and classical models based on deployment scale: classical remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried workloads. Can fail if the deployment is small or infrequently queried (pretraining never amortizes), if the gradient-free criterion underperforms on data outside the 25-task benchmark, or if undetected accuracy regressions appear on domain-specific series.
rationale: With a single 24 GB GPU and a limited budget, a gradient-free single-block removal is cheap to apply, requires no retraining, and directly lowers inference cost and latency while preserving zero-shot performance, making Chronos-2 viable for large or frequently queried deployments where its pretraining cost amortizes within months.
technique: Gradient-free structured pruning of TSFM encoder blocks
